## Importing Dataset

TLDR (written by KAK): These data represent a comprehensive study combining biological Selenium (Se) accumulation in a variety of organisms across trophic levels and chemical characterisation of water and sediment in the Kootenai River of Montana. Samples were collected from three semi-annual sampling events (Fall 2020, Spring 2021, and Fall 2021). 

Data availability: https://www.sciencebase.gov/catalog/item/62881e4dd34e4fef2ec3c334

Summary (written by USGS): This dataset includes analyses of selenium (Se) in water, sediment, periphyton, and benthic invertebrate and fish tissues from the Kootenai River in Idaho and Montana. The samples were collected as part of a study intended to evaluate selenium distribution and bioaccumulation in the aquatic food webs of the Kootenai River. This dataset includes complete food web sample results from our first three semi-annual sampling events (fall 2020, spring 2021, and fall 2021), in addition to more limited data from September 2018-2023 (mainly water sample results). Samples were collected from four sites on the Kootenai River between Libby Dam, Montana, and the border between Idaho, USA, and British Columbia, Canada. Sites were located at about 1, 81, 105, and 185 kilometers (km) downstream from Libby Dam. An additional comparison sampling site was on Lake Creek, near Troy, Montana.

The water samples were analyzed for dissolved Se and Se species, including selenite, selenate, selenocyanate, methylseleninic acid, selenomethionine, and unknown Se species. Sediment samples were collected by scooping from depositional areas in shallow, quiescent water near the river edge. Sediment samples were sieved (63 micron pore size Nitex fabric) and analyzed for Se. Three types of periphyton and suspended particulates were sampled: periphyton scraped from rocks (PRS), periphyton grown on glass microscope slides (PSL), and suspended particulate material on flow-through filters (SPM). For invertebrates, whole-body tissues were analyzed from 43 distinct benthic invertebrate taxa, and multiple tissues were additionally analyzed for one taxon, the western pearlshell mussel, Margaritifera falcata. Five fish species were targeted for repeat sampling: mountain whitefish (Prosopium williamsoni), rainbow trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss), slimy sculpin (Cottus cognatus), redside shiner (Richardsonius balteatus), and northern pikeminnow (Ptychocheilus oregonensis). Occasional samples were also obtained from 4 additional species: kokanee (Oncorhynchus nerka), brown trout (Salmo trutta), longnose sucker (Catostomus catostomus), and largescale sucker (Catostomus macrocheilus). Fish were sometimes analyzed for whole body selenium concentrations, or dissected for separate analyses of muscle, liver, egg-ovary tissues, and the carcass (everything leftover after the other tissues were removed). The specific tissue samples removed and analyzed varied by the sex and size of the fish, sampling event, and specific objectives. The total sample counts included in this dataset are 292 water sample results from 83 water samples, 27 sediment results, 114 periphyton results, 343 benthic invertebrate results, and 1,448 fish tissue results from 524 individual fish. Most analyses in the present dataset were for selenium with some additional analyses of mercury (Hg).

```{r sp_dict wrangle}
#Importing Species Dictionary
sp_dict <- read_excel("Data/Raw/USGS_All_Data_Tables.xlsx",
```

# Question 3: Does Se concentration differ between tissue types in Mountain Whitefish?
## Hypotheses
H0: mean ln(Se) is equal in muscle, liver, and egg:  mu_muscle = mu_liver = mu_egg
       (i.e., the geometric mean Se does not differ among tissues)
Ha: at least one tissue differs.
alpha = 0.05; post hoc pairwise contrasts with Tukey/Holm adjustment.

```{r 3a_Tissue data wrangling}
se_tissue <- bio_processed |>
  filter(
    simplified_sample_type == "fish",
    analyte == "Se",
    reporting_basis == "dw",
    sample_matrix %in% c("Fish_EGG", "Fish_LVR", "Fish_MSC", "Fish_TST")  # CAR and WB excluded: whole-body burden, not specific tissues
  )
# number of measurements per species
se_tissue |>
  count(species_id, sample_matrix) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = sample_matrix, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)

# tissue combinations per MWF fish (before QA filters)
se_tissue |>
  filter(species_id == "MWF") |>
  distinct(usgs_universal_id, sample_matrix) |>
  group_by(usgs_universal_id) |>
  summarise(tissues = paste(sort(sample_matrix), collapse = "+"), .groups = "drop") |>
  count(tissues, sort = TRUE) #checking for sufficient tissue type unique samples in MWF. n= 69 obs have all three tissue types if excluding TST (n = 4).

# ---- MWF_tissue: ALL MWF fish with at least one of the three tissues ----
MWF_tissue <- se_tissue |>
  filter(species_id == "MWF",
         sample_matrix %in% c("Fish_EGG", "Fish_LVR", "Fish_MSC"),
         sample_qaqc_qualifier == "--",
         results_calculation == "raw") |>
  mutate(fish_id = factor(usgs_universal_id),
         tissue  = factor(sample_matrix,
                          levels = c("Fish_MSC", "Fish_LVR", "Fish_EGG"),
                          labels = c("Muscle", "Liver", "Egg")),
         site_id = factor(site_id),
         se      = result_value_mg_kg)

stopifnot(!any(duplicated(MWF_tissue[c("fish_id", "tissue")])))  # one row per fish x tissue

n_distinct(MWF_tissue$fish_id)   # fish with >= 1 tissue (all filters applied)

# ---- tissue_df: fish with ALL three tissues (complete cases) ----

complete_ids <- MWF_tissue |>
  distinct(fish_id, tissue) |>
  count(fish_id) |>
  filter(n == 3) |>
  pull(fish_id)

tissue_df <- MWF_tissue |>
  filter(fish_id %in% complete_ids) |>
  droplevels() |>
  select(fish_id, tissue, se, everything(),
         -usgs_universal_id, -sample_matrix, -result_value_mg_kg)

n_distinct(tissue_df$fish_id)    # no. of fish with complete cases
nrow(tissue_df)                  # no. of observations

levels(tissue_df$tissue)

#write_csv(tissue_df, "tissue_df.csv")

```

```{r 3b Tissue Descriptive Stats}
               locations = cells_body(columns = n, rows = tissue == "All tissues (pooled)")) |>
  tab_header(title = "Se in Mountain Whitefish tissues (n = 54 fish, 3 tissues each)")

tissue_summ_table
```

## Water Stuff

### Datasets

```{r water_dataset}

# Importing raw datasets
water_raw <- read_csv("Data/Raw/USGS_Se_Raw_Water_Data.csv", skip = 1) %>% 
  janitor::clean_names()

# Import location data
location_dict <- read_excel("Data/Raw/USGS_All_Data_Tables.xlsx",
    sheet = "Table2_Site-Dictionary",
    skip = 1) %>% 
  janitor::clean_names()

# Initial data wrangling

sediment_holder <- bio_processed %>% 
  filter(simplified_sample_type == "sediment",
         results_calculation != "average") %>% 
  select(usgs_universal_id:site_id, date, analyte, results_calculation, result_value_mg_kg) %>% 
  mutate(analyte = case_when(analyte == "Se" ~ "Se(part)"),
         site_id = case_when(site_id == "KR13D" ~ "KR13",
                             .default = site_id))

water_processed <- water_raw %>%
  mutate(date = mdy(sample_date)) %>%            # format dates
  filter(sample_type == "Environmental",
         analyte != "Hg") %>%           
  left_join(location_dict, by = "site_id") %>%   # join lat/long data
  select(date, usgs_site_number, site_name,      # select relevant columns
        site_id, sample_type:qualifiers, 
        latitude, longitude) %>% 
  mutate(usgs_site_number = case_when(usgs_site_number == "12307750" ~ "12309500",
                                      usgs_site_number == "12303500" ~ "12304500",
                                      usgs_site_number == "12301919" ~ "12301933",
                                      .default = usgs_site_number)) %>% 
  full_join(sediment_processed)

```

The original dataset contained three USGS sites that did not contain any gauge data (12307750, 12304500, and 12301933). These three sites were matched to the next closest USGS gauge station with at least discharge data available.

Qualifiers:
U - Result is < MDL
J - > MDL but < MRL
Z - idk but I think its okay to overlook it


Daily data
00060: Discharge
00065: Gage height
00010: Water temperature [degC]
00400: pH
00095: specific conductance [uS/cm]

Continuous data
00300: dissolve oxygen [mg/L]
32321: Pycocyanin relative fluorescence [RFU]
63680: turbidity
32315: Chlorophyll relative fluorescence [RFU]


```{r usgs_daily_data}

# Daily average of discharge, gage, temperature, pH, and specific conductance from daily data

usgs_daily_raw <- 
  
  read_waterdata_daily(
  monitoring_location_id = c("USGS-12301933", "USGS-12302055", "USGS-12304500",
                             "USGS-12305000", "USGS-12307750", "USGS-12310100",
                             "USGS-12322000", "USGS-12303500", "USGS-12301919"),
  parameter_code = c("00060", "00065", "00010", "00400", "00095"),
  time = c("2018-03-28", "2023-09-14"))

# Processed

usgs_daily_processed <- usgs_daily_raw %>% 
  mutate(year = year(time),
         month = month(time),
         day = day(time),
         season = case_when(month %in% c(3,4,5) ~ "Spring",
                            month %in% c(8,9,10) ~ "Fall")) %>% 
  na.omit(season) %>% 
  separate_wider_delim(
    cols = monitoring_location_id, 
    delim = "USGS-", 
    names = c("holder", "usgs_site_number")) %>%
  mutate(parameter = case_when(parameter_code == "00060" ~ "discharge",
                               parameter_code == "00065" ~ "gage_height",
                               parameter_code == "00010" ~ "temperature",
                               parameter_code == "00400" ~ "pH",
                               parameter_code == "00095" ~ "specific_conductance")) %>% 
  group_by(year, season, usgs_site_number, parameter) %>% 
  summarise(mean = mean(value)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = parameter, values_from = mean) %>% 
  select(-pH)

```

```{r usgs_cont_ph}

# Daily average of pH from continuous data

usgs_cont_ph_raw <- rbind(
  
  read_waterdata_continuous(
  monitoring_location_id = c("USGS-12301933", "USGS-12302055", "USGS-12304500",
                             "USGS-12305000", "USGS-12307750", "USGS-12310100",
                             "USGS-12322000", "USGS-12303500", "USGS-12301919"),
  parameter_code = c("00400"), time = c("2018-03-28", "2019-03-27")),
  
  read_waterdata_continuous(
  monitoring_location_id = c("USGS-12301933", "USGS-12302055", "USGS-12304500",
                             "USGS-12305000", "USGS-12307750", "USGS-12310100",
                             "USGS-12322000", "USGS-12303500", "USGS-12301919"),
  parameter_code = c("00400"), time = c("2019-03-28", "2021-09-14")),
  
  read_waterdata_continuous(
  monitoring_location_id = c("USGS-12301933", "USGS-12302055", "USGS-12304500",
                             "USGS-12305000", "USGS-12307750", "USGS-12310100",
                             "USGS-12322000", "USGS-12303500", "USGS-12301919"),
  parameter_code = c("00400"), time = c("2021-09-15", "2023-09-14")))

# Processed

usgs_cont_ph_processed <- usgs_cont_ph_raw %>% 
  mutate(date = as.Date(time),
         year = year(time),
         month = month(time),
         day = day(time)) %>% 
  separate_wider_delim(
  cols = monitoring_location_id, 
  delim = "USGS-", 
  names = c("holder", "usgs_site_number")) %>% 
  mutate(parameter = case_when(parameter_code == "00400" ~ "pH")) %>% 
  group_by(year, month, day, usgs_site_number, parameter) %>% 
  summarise(mean = mean(value)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = parameter, values_from = mean) %>% 
  mutate(date = make_date(year = year, month = month, day = day),
         season = case_when(month %in% c(3,4,5) ~ "Spring",
                            month %in% c(8,9,10) ~ "Fall")) %>% 
  filter(season %in% c("Fall", "Spring")) %>% 
  arrange(year, month, day)

```

```{r usgs_cont_minors}
  monitoring_location_id = c("USGS-12301933", "USGS-12302055", "USGS-12304500",

                             "USGS-12322000", "USGS-12303500", "USGS-12301919"),
  parameter_code = c("32315"),
  time = c("2020-09-28", "2021-09-28")),

  read_waterdata_continuous(
  monitoring_location_id = c("USGS-12301933", "USGS-12302055", "USGS-12304500",
                             "USGS-12305000", "USGS-12307750", "USGS-12310100",
                             "USGS-12322000", "USGS-12303500", "USGS-12301919"),
  parameter_code = c("32315"),
  time = c("2021-09-29", "2022-09-14")),

  read_waterdata_continuous(
  monitoring_location_id = c("USGS-12301933", "USGS-12302055", "USGS-12304500",
                             "USGS-12305000", "USGS-12307750", "USGS-12310100",
                             "USGS-12322000", "USGS-12303500", "USGS-12301919"),
  parameter_code = c("32315"),
  time = c("2022-09-15", "2023-09-14")))

# Processed

usgs_cont_metabolism_processed <- usgs_cont_metabolism_raw %>% 
  mutate(date = as.Date(time),
         year = year(time),
         month = month(time),
         day = day(time)) %>% 
  separate_wider_delim(
    cols = monitoring_location_id, 
    delim = "USGS-", 
    names = c("holder", "usgs_site_number")) %>% 
  mutate(parameter = case_when(parameter_code == "32315" ~ "chlorophyll")) %>% 
  group_by(year, month, day, usgs_site_number, parameter) %>% 
  summarise(mean = mean(value)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = parameter, values_from = mean) %>% 
  mutate(date = make_date(year = year, month = month, day = day),
         season = case_when(month %in% c(3,4,5) ~ "Spring",
                            month %in% c(8,9,10) ~ "Fall")) %>% 
  filter(season %in% c("Fall", "Spring")) %>% 
  arrange(year, month, day)

usgs_cont_minors_processed <- usgs_cont_minors_raw %>% 
  mutate(date = as.Date(time),
         year = year(time),
         month = month(time),
         day = day(time)) %>% 
  separate_wider_delim(
  cols = monitoring_location_id, 
  delim = "USGS-", 
  names = c("holder", "usgs_site_number")) %>% 
  mutate(parameter = case_when(parameter_code == "32321" ~ "phycocyanin",
                               parameter_code == "00300" ~ "dis_oxygen",
                               parameter_code == "63680" ~ "turbidity")) %>% 
  group_by(year, month, day, usgs_site_number, parameter) %>% 
  summarise(mean = mean(value)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = parameter, values_from = mean) %>% 
  mutate(date = make_date(year = year, month = month, day = day),
         season = case_when(month %in% c(3,4,5) ~ "Spring",
                            month %in% c(8,9,10) ~ "Fall")) %>% 
  filter(season %in% c("Fall", "Spring")) %>% 
  select(-phycocyanin) %>% 
  arrange(year, month, day)

```

### Exploration, Visualization, and Data Summaries

```{r water_data_exploration}

# Summary stats of processed data

water_processed_stats <- water_processed %>% 
  summarise(length(site_name),
            n_distinct(usgs_site_number),
            n_distinct(site_name),
            n_distinct(analyte),
            n_distinct(year(date))) %>%
  mutate(perc_MDL = round((count(water_processed %>% filter(str_detect(qualifiers, "U")))/nrow(water_processed))*100, 2))

# Summary statistics for dissolved Se concentrations in water samples from the Kootenai River watershed study area by season (across all study years, 2018-2023)
se_speciation_watershed_seasonal <- water_processed %>%
  mutate(year = year(date),
         month = month(date),
         season = case_when(month %in% c(3,4,5) ~ "Spring",
                            month %in% c(8,9,10) ~ "Fall")) %>% 
  na.omit(season) %>% 
  group_by(analyte, season) %>% 
  summarise(n = length(result),
            minimum = min(result),
            q25 = quantile(result, probs = 0.25),
            mean = round(mean(result), 4),
            median = median(result),
            q75 = quantile(result, probs = 0.75),
            maximum = max(result)) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 2)))

# Summed dissolved Se speciation in water samples in the Kootenai River watershed and percentage of total dissolved Se concentration in 2021
se_speciation_site_2021 <- water_processed %>% 
  filter(year(date) == "2022",
         analyte != "Se(part)") %>% 
  mutate(year = year(date),
         month = month(date),
         season = case_when(month %in% c(3,4,5) ~ "Spring",
                            month %in% c(8,9,10) ~ "Fall")) %>% 
  na.omit(season) %>% 
  group_by(site_name, analyte, season) %>% 
  summarise(total = sum(result, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  filter(season =="Spring")


se_speciation_site_2021_plot <- ggplot(se_speciation_site_2021,
                                       aes(x = site_name, y = total, fill = analyte)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill", stat = "identity") +
  labs(title = "Selenium Speciation by Site", 
       subtitle = "Spring 2021",
       x = "", y = "Percentage", 
       fill = "Species") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, vjust = 1, hjust = 1),
        legend.position = "right")
se_speciation_site_2021_plot

# Summed dissolved and suspended Se speciation in water samples in the Kootenai River watershed with sediment data and percentage of total dissolved Se concentration in 2021

se_full_speciation_site_2021 <- water_processed %>% 
  filter(year(date) == "2021",
         site_id %in% c("KR13", "KR2", "KR6", "KR9.2", "LC")) %>% 
  mutate(year = year(date),
         month = month(date),
         season = case_when(month %in% c(3,4,5) ~ "Spring",
                            month %in% c(8,9,10) ~ "Fall")) %>%
  group_by(site_name, analyte, season, date, year, month) %>% 
  summarise(total = sum(result, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup()

# Total dissolved Se concentrations in water samples from the Kootenai River watershed study area in the Spring
world <- water_processed %>% 
  mutate(year = year(date),
         month = month(date),
         season = case_when(month %in% c(3,4,5) ~ "Spring",
                            month %in% c(8,9,10) ~ "Fall")) %>% 
  na.omit(season) %>% 
  select(month, year, season, site_name, site_id, analyte, result) %>%

  ungroup() %>% 
  arrange(year) %>% 
  #filter(season == "Spring") %>%

```

### Linear Model

Can dissolved Se concentration be predicted by water quality parameters?

Available water quality parameters are: 00060: Discharge, 00065: Gage height, 00010: Water temperature [degC], 00400: pH, 00095: specific conductance [uS/cm], 00300: dissolve oxygen [mg/L], 00045: precipitation [in], 63680: turbidity

Data were averaged over the Spring and Fall months defined.

```{r linear_model_dataset}

water_usgs_df <- usgs_cont_metabolism_processed %>%
  full_join(usgs_cont_ph_processed,
            by = c("usgs_site_number", "date", "year", "month", "day", "season")) %>%
  full_join(usgs_cont_minors_processed,
            by = c("usgs_site_number", "date", "year", "month", "day", "season")) %>%
  full_join(usgs_cont_metabolism_processed,
            by = c("usgs_site_number", "date", "year", "month", "day", "season", "chlorophyll"))

water_se <- water_processed %>% 
  mutate(year = year(date),
         month = month(date),
         day = day(date),
         season = case_when(month %in% c(3,4,5) ~ "Spring",
                            month %in% c(8,9,10) ~ "Fall")) %>% 
  na.omit(season) %>%
  select(date, year, month, day, season, site_name, site_id, usgs_site_number, analyte, result) %>% 
  group_by(site_name, year, month, day, date, season, usgs_site_number) %>%
  summarise(total_se = sum(result, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  arrange(year) %>% 
  left_join(usgs_daily_processed, by = c("usgs_site_number", "year", "season")) %>% 
  left_join(water_usgs_df, by = c("usgs_site_number", "year", "month", "day", "season", "date"))

```
